The targeted Research and Development (R&D) advance assurance pilot launched on 18 May 2026.

Read the guidance to check if your client can apply for either targeted advance assurance or full claim advance assurance for their R&D tax relief claim.

HMRC is making it easier for companies and their agents to find information about advance assurance services for R&D tax relief.

From 12 October 2026, HMRC staff working in R&D will include a short signpost to advance assurance guidance in their external email signatures. The same information will also appear in the automatic reply from the main R&D compliance mailbox.

These signposts will raise awareness of both HMRC’s targeted and full claim advance assurance services and help businesses access the right support when needed.

The targeted advance assurance pilot is available to eligible small and medium sized enterprises seeking certainty on up to 2 specific areas of an R&D tax relief claim before submission. If granted, assurances are valid for the duration of the R&D project, for a maximum of 5 years.

The full claim advance assurance is available to eligible small and medium sized enterprises making their first R&D claim. It provides clarity on the full claim, and if granted, can cover up to 3 accounting periods.

New process to speed up National Insurance refunds

Since early summer, HMRC has been using a new automated payment process to help issue National Insurance refunds more quickly.

Where HMRC identifies that someone may have overpaid National Insurance contributions, we will send them a letter with details of their employment and contributions. They should check the information and either confirm it is correct or tell us if anything needs to be updated.

Customers can respond online through GOV.UK or by updating and returning the form attached to the letter. HMRC is urging customers receiving such a letter not to ignore it.

We want customers to feel confident when dealing with HMRC. You can quickly check if a letter you have received from HMRC is genuine.

This provides reassurance to customers that they are responding to genuine HMRC communications, helping them to identify and avoid fraudsters. HMRC refund notifications will never ask customers to click on links.

A simpler way to check current service problems

We are improving how we publish information about service problems on GOV.UK. Our new live service issues page brings all current service problems together in one place, making it easier to find the latest information when a service is unavailable.

A link from the existing service availability pages directs you to the new page, helping ensure service information remains easy to find through the routes agents already use.

The new page allows us to update information more quickly when issues affect multiple services, giving you faster access to the latest position. It also helps to make sure information is consistent across services and provides a clearer route to live updates. This will help to quickly understand whether a problem may be affecting your clients or the task you are trying to complete.

You can also sign up to get notified about service availability page updates by selecting ’Get emails about this page’.

Providing feedback on HMRC manuals

HMRC manuals contain technical guidance for HMRC staff and tax professionals. Their primary purpose is to explain HMRC’s interpretation of relevant legislation, which is the basis on which the department makes decisions.

To tell us whether a page is useful, suggest improvements or report a problem with a page, you can use the:

feedback routes in the footer of all pages on GOV.UK

contact GOV.UK form

The HMRC manuals team review all items of feedback on HMRC manuals from internal and external users.

Within the last 12 months we received 1,470 feedback comments and 60% led to guidance improvements. However, the volume is still low compared to the overall usage. Help us improve the content by providing feedback, even if it is to indicate that a page is useful.

Agent engagement

Help us improve GOV.UK guidance

HMRC is looking for agents who support small business customers with business expenses.

If you would like to give us your feedback, complete the survey form.

Take part in this research to help us improve the experience. As a thank you, you will have the choice to enter a draw for a chance to be randomly selected to receive a voucher worth £75.

Taking part is voluntary.

Any information you share will be:

anonymised

kept confidential

used only for research purposes

held securely at all times in line with data protection law

Technical updates and reminders

Developments and changes to legislation and allowances relating to UK tax, including:

Tax

Company Tax Returns — filing reminders

Inheritance Tax on pensions — prepare for changes from 6 April 2027

Voluntary registration for non-mandatory payrolling of benefits in kind

Making Tax Digital

Get ready for the next Making Tax Digital for Income Tax deadline on 7 November

HMRC agent services

Tax on bank and building society interest 2026

Multi-factor authentication — now live on all agent accounts

Self Assessment — help your clients file early

Talk Money Week — take action with the HMRC app

Tax adviser registration — temporary pause to agent reference number checks

Research and Development tax relief update — advanced assurance services

New process to speed up National Insurance refunds

A simpler way to check current service problems

Providing feedback on HMRC manuals

Agent engagement

Help us improve GOV.UK guidance

Tax

Company Tax Returns — filing reminders

To help HMRC process your clients’ tax returns without delay:

check that the start and end dates of the return period you are filing are correct and that they match your client’s accounting period structure

make sure that supporting documents filed with the CT600 tax return such as computations and accounts are in the correct format

wait at least 24 hours before trying to amend a submitted return

check the company’s bank details (BACS) before filing the CT600 tax return and include them on any amended return for the same period

do not tick box 45, ‘repayment for an earlier period’, unless you are making a loss carry back claim or a claim under section 458 of the Corporation Tax Act 2010

Claiming relief for losses carried back

When submitting your clients’ Company Tax Return, include the most up to date bank details on the CT600.

If the CT600 includes a loss carry back claim, you must tick box 45 to show that a repayment for an earlier or prior accounting period is due.

Read more information on completing the CT600 tax return.

If ticking box 45, provide a breakdown of the claim in your computations to show how losses are to be used. This is particularly important for terminal loss claims.

When electing to carry losses back under section 37 of the Corporation Tax Act 2010, make sure to carry all available losses back to extinguish profits of the previous accounting periods before carrying remaining losses forward. Failure to do so will result in HMRC being unable to process your client’s claim.

If making a loss carry back claim, do not:

submit an amended CT600 for the same accounting period if it contains the same information

submit an amended CT600 for the accounting period receiving the loss

submit an original CT600 by post, as all Company Tax Returns must be filed online through Government Gateway

You must submit an amended CT600 if:

the return includes changes other than the loss carry back claim

the loss carry back claim itself needs to be amended

Inheritance Tax on pensions — prepare for changes from 6 April 2027

From 6 April 2027, most unused pension funds and pension death benefits will be included in the value of a deceased person’s estate for Inheritance Tax (IHT) purposes. These changes were announced at Autumn Budget 2024 and are included in the Finance Act 2026.

What you need to do

You should prepare for the changes if you advise:

personal representatives

pension beneficiaries

pension scheme administrators

The changes apply when a pension scheme member dies on or after 6 April 2027.

You should familiarise yourself with the 2 technical notes linked in the next section and consider how the reforms may affect your clients and working arrangements.

Technical notes

The Inheritance Tax on pensions: technical note explains:

how notional pension property will be identified, valued and allocated

who will report and pay any IHT due

the use of withholding notices and the pensions direct payment scheme

how the reforms interact with Income Tax rules on pension death benefits

The Inheritance Tax on pensions: technical note 2 provides additional detail on:

information sharing requirements

withholding notices

pensions direct payment scheme notices and clearance

Guidance and other supporting materials will be updated and published by April 2027.

Voluntary registration for non-mandatory payrolling of benefits in kind

From November 2026, employers can register to voluntarily payroll non-mandated benefits for the 2027 to 2028 tax year, using the payrolling benefits and expenses online service.

From 6 April 2027, employers who voluntarily choose to payroll benefits in kind that are not part of the first phase of mandatory payrolling must also pay Class 1A National Insurance contributions through payroll. They will no longer be able to report these separately at the end of the tax year. They will also not be able to payroll the Income Tax and report the associated Class 1A National Insurance contributions separately.

Customers who have already registered to voluntarily payroll will automatically continue for the 2027 to 2028 tax year. Customers who decide to stop voluntary payrolling non-mandated benefits must withdraw by 5 April 2027.

Employers with eligible globally mobile employees (GME) will be exempt from mandatory payrolling of benefits in kind and expenses. This is due to the practical difficulties in real time payroll reporting. Employers with eligible GME need to submit an online G-form. This will be made available in November 2026 and will help to inform HMRC which employees should be excluded.

Voluntary registration information will be included in the updated guidance on Mandatory payrolling of benefits in kind and expenses – interim guidance and legislation.

Making Tax Digital

Get ready for the next Making Tax Digital for Income Tax deadline on 7 November 2026
